title: Hobbies & Free Time
description: Name hobbies and describe regular free-time activities.
objectives: Name hobbies and describe regular free-time activities.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to name hobbies and describe regular free-time activities. The central language is like plus noun or to-infinitive. It belongs to the practical context of free time & abilities. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: I like to read after dinner.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the hobbies & free time exchange.

blocks.english: We play games on the weekend.
blocks.explanation: This hobbies & free time model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you like to do?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the hobbies & free time exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I like to read after dinner.” and “We play games on the weekend.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: like plus noun or to-infinitive.

Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
